plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing a profitable opportunity. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) when I win, there's no incentive to shade my bid. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my value of $31, regardless of my beliefs about Betty and Charles's strategies.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because your payment only depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win), so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable trades. Since this holds true irrespective of what others do, I will bid exactly my value of $22.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it doesn't depend on beliefs about others' bids, since you pay the second price regardless. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since my value is $40, the optimal bid, maximizing expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies, is to bid exactly $40.
